headline: South Asia: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
- Persian Gulf Region: Can Yemen’s government forces sustain their offensive against the Houthis?.
- Africa: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, one day ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attack leaves Vinnytsia without power.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russian attack leaves Vinnytsia without power.
Vinnytsia Mayor Serhii Morhunov says the damage is being assessed following Russian strikes. Critical infrastructure is operating on backup power and additional buses and minibuses will replace electric public transport.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian airstrikes on Kherson kill ambulance driver and injure civilians, including children.
A 64-year-old emergency medical services driver has suffered fatal injuries following Russian airstrikes on Kherson. Thirteen people have been injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russia attacks Ukraine with Iskander, Kalibr and Kh-22/32 missiles and over 300 drones: air defences downs 293 aerial assets.
Russia launched ballistic and cruise missiles and 332 attack drones overnight. Ukraine's air defences destroyed 293 aerial assets, while impacts were recorded at 22 locations.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians strike Sumy and Sumy Oblast with guided bombs: residential area hit, two injured – photos.
Russian forces attacked Sumy and Sumy Oblast with guided aerial bombs on Saturday morning, hitting a residential area and injuring two people.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Wer führt in Zukunft die SPD? Mit Rasmus Buchsteiner.
Es war eine Chaoswoche für den Kanzler Friedrich Merz. Das Rentenpaket entwickelt sich zur weiteren Zerreißprobe für die Koalition. Der neue Arbeitsminister Alexander Schweitzer macht es für den Kanzler nicht einfacher. Warum der SPD-Pragmatiker plötzlich auf Konfrontation geht und wie diese Machtkämpfe die Regierungsarbeit lähmen, steht im Zentrum der Analyse. Gleichzeitig brodelt es an der […]
- Politico Europe, 22 hours ago: Zelenskyy warns 20M Ukrainians could flee to Europe if Russia wins war.
The stark warning comes as Kyiv heads into a brutal winter and faces a cash crunch.
- Politico Europe, 22 hours ago: Denmark, Italy, Poland urge EU leaders to harden stance on irregular migration.
Draft conclusions backed by Rome, Warsaw and Copenhagen say irregular migration is "negatively linked to crime rates."

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Can Yemen’s government forces sustain their offensive against the Houthis?.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Can Yemen’s government forces sustain their offensive against the Houthis?.
Houthi missile strikes threaten key supply routes on Yemen's Red Sea coast, intensifying pressure on government forces.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Iran giving Yemen's Houthis target intelligence for drone, missile strikes on Saudi Arabia - report.
Adam Baron, a Yemen expert and fellow with Washington-based policy institute New America, told the WSJ that the recent Houthi military gains were "undeniably" based on external Iranian assistance.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: US lawmakers condemn settler violence after Washington Post journalist wounded in West Bank clashes.
While the Israeli condemnations largely called for further investigation to determine the facts, US and Palestinian condemnations accused Israeli settlers of having attacked Levine.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Sudan’s army claims dozens of RSF fighters killed in Nyala attack.
Rapid Support Forces accuse army of killing 30 civilians in attack on Nyala's busy livestock market.
Africa - bottom line: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
- Africanews, 22 hours ago: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia.
Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.
Iran has denied any involvement in an escalation of attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi targets. The international airport in Yemen’s interim capital Aden was struck by two missiles late on Friday, the second such incident in less than two weeks.
- Africanews, 19 hours ago: Ethiopian gains in Tigray risk wider war with Eritrea, analyst warns.
Ethiopia’s military advances in northern Tigray do not spell an end to the conflict but have the potential to increase the risk of war with neighboring Eritrea, an analyst with knowledge of the region has warned
- Africanews, 18 hours ago: Rights group says eastern Libyan authorities are carrying out executions.
Human Rights Watch says the military has killed an estimated 31 people since late August, with at least 50 other people at risk.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine. The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.
- The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the U.S.-Russia diesel deal a “weak decision” that would help Moscow prolong the war, as Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed three children among the dead
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: North Korea says tested AI-assisted torpedo system.
North Korea has tested a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state media reported Saturday, as the nuclear-armed country steps up weapons testing. The announcement came days after Pyongyang said it had test-fired two types of cruise missiles from a submarine after weeks of friction with Seoul over a landmine explosion along their border.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Any miscalculation by adversaries will invite response beyond their ‘imagination, calculation’, warns CNSC.
Commander National Strategic Command (CNSC) General Aamer Raza warned the country’s adversaries on Saturday that “any miscalculation will be met with a response far beyond the imagination or the calculation of the initiator”. “To those who harbour hostile designs across our borders, our stance remains resolute and unambiguous. There is no space for conflict or war in a nuclearised environment and any miscalculation will be met with a response far beyond the imagination or calculation of the initiator,” warned the commander of Pakistan’s strategic command.
Asia - bottom line: Oregon teen gunman was tackled by ‘heroic’ teacher then shot by students’ father.
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Oregon teen gunman was tackled by ‘heroic’ teacher then shot by students’ father.
A teacher threw her phone at the teenage gunman who killed four people at an Oregon junior school, then tackled and fought with him – probably saving lives before he was shot by a father who followed him into the building, police said Friday. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz called the teacher’s actions “heroic” during a news conference and said she was not injured. He identified the attacker as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II and said all of the victims were shot in the same classroom. Authorities...
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Asean’s Myanmar peace push needs Japan’s ‘silent diplomacy’.
Japan has long established itself as a pioneer of mediation in Southeast Asia. In 1990, for example, its officials helped broker talks between Cambodia’s warring factions, supplementing international efforts to end conflict in the country. Now, Tokyo is seeking to upgrade its diplomatic toolkit. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ International Peace Mediation Unit was set up in March, followed by the launch of the Parliamentary Association for Peace Mediation in May. Around the same time, the...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: UK deports Romanian convicted of arson at ex-PM Starmer’s homes.
Britain has deported a Romanian man jailed for two years in June for arson attacks on two properties linked to then British prime minister Keir Starmer, the interior ministry said Saturday. Ukraine-born Stanislav Carpiuc was found guilty of the attacks alongside Ukrainian citizen Roman Lavrynovych, who was jailed for seven years over the May 2025 attacks on two London houses and a vehicle. “This individual has now been deported from the UK,” a Home Office spokesperson said, without indicating...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Corrupt officials have nowhere to hide, China’s anti-graft watchdog warns.
There is “no way out” for corrupt officials no matter how senior they are, China’s top anti-corruption watchdog has warned following the downfall of a former big-city mayor who survived numerous previous scandals. This week, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) announced both the probe into Huang Qifan, the former mayor of Chongqing, and the expulsion of a senior figure in Sichuan province. On Saturday, the commission said these developments showed the party’s “unwavering...
India - bottom line: Australian couple, 85 and 82, restore 970 hectares after 20 years of work.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Australian couple, 85 and 82, restore 970 hectares after 20 years of work.
In their eighties, Ken and Jill Hooper have become dedicated stewards of bushland in Australia, showcasing an inspiring commitment to conservation post-retirement. Over the last twenty years, after acquiring properties in Victoria and New South Wales, they focus on enhancing biodiversity and curbing invasive species to safeguard native wildlife. Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Iran helping Houthis: How Tehran is hitting Saudi Arabia without fighting directly.
Iran's backing of Yemen's Houthi rebels has intensified, providing crucial intelligence and military guidance against Saudi Arabia. This partnership has evolved into a robust military collaboration involving advanced weaponry training, drone development, and missile production. Analysts emphasize that this Iranian support has significantly empowered the Houthis in their ongoing conflict. The increasing influence of Tehran raises substantial security concerns in the region, prompting regional leaders to reevaluate their strategies.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: 1 Killed, 3 Injured As Truck Hits Bikes In Delhi's Dwarka, Driver Arrested.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Strong 6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: S. Korean envoy condemns Houthi attacks, calls for stronger U.N. sanctions to block weapons supplies.
- Yonhap News Agency, 19 hours ago: S. Korean envoy condemns Houthi attacks, calls for stronger U.N. sanctions to block weapons supplies.
WASHINGTON, Oct. 16 (Yonhap) -- South Korea has condemned recent deadly attacks ...

SEOUL, Oct. 17 (Yonhap) -- The South Korean government expressed regret Saturday...
- Yonhap News Agency, 20 hours ago: Pyongyang rejects Seoul's hypersonic test claims, justifies own arms buildup.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Magnitude-3.0 aftershock strikes near Leongatha, south-east of Melbourne.
- ABC News Australia, 6 hours ago: Magnitude-3.0 aftershock strikes near Leongatha, south-east of Melbourne.
South-eastern Victoria has been slightly shaken by an earthquake aftershock, three weeks after an overnight tremor woke thousands.
- The Guardian - Australia, 8 hours ago: Mexican judge sentences three men to 158 years in prison for murders of Australian and US surfers​.
Australian ​brothers Jake ​and Callum Robinson, and ​their ‌American friend Carter Rhoad, were killed while on a surf trip in Baja California in 2024 Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast A Mexican ⁠judge ⁠has sentenced ​three men to 158 years ⁠and nine months in prison each for ⁠the murder of ​two Australian ‌brothers ‌and their American friend during ‌a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California.
- ABC News Australia, 8 hours ago: Dogs captured after attack on Brisbane man.
Emergency services were called to Kittyhawk Drive in Chermside just after 6pm on Friday following reports a man had been attacked by dogs.
- The Guardian - Australia, 21 hours ago: ‘That bridge almost broke our mob’: the Ngarrindjeri warrior women and the fight to preserve sacred knowledge.
A new documentary tells the story of the Hindmarsh Island Bridge affair and the clash between cultural rights and property developers’ ambitions Warning: This article contains images and names of Indigenous Australians who have died There’s a bridge in South Australia, about 300 metres of concrete and steel, that sparked an extraordinary, decades-long saga of heartbreak, skulduggery and vindication. Millionaire developers, academics, state and federal governments, the media and the courts all played roles in what would become known as the Hindmarsh Island Bridge affair. Continue reading...
